clue.text: Person using lawyer, say, securing legal right in court

indicators.note: the court abbreviation holds the legal right firmly inside it

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A litigant who has hired a lawyer is trying to establish a legal right before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who engages a solicitor or barrister is that professional's customer, the usual word for whom is this one.

clue.text: A search after pet in grave situation

indicators.note: the search phrase follows the pet in the answer

parts.note: a cat is a pet
taken as written
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A frantic hunt for a lost cat in a dire position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave situation' sounds like a crisis, but it is literally a place where graves are.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery of tunnels with burial niches is a place where graves are located.

clue.text: Pressure showing in, for example, cricket test

indicators.note: the pressure letter goes inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

explanation.surface: Pressure tells in a cricket Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the chirping creature, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely, checking its condition, is to look it over carefully.

clue.text: Wicked and so unfair, wrongfully imprisoning European

indicators.note: the shuffled letters lock the European letter inside
the letters are put together wrongly, so reshuffled

parts.note: these eight letters are the fodder that gets rearranged

explanation.surface: It is so unjust and evil to lock up a European without due cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A villainous, criminal or evil scheme is described with this word.

clue.text: Put together a score, not 27

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wrote a piece of music
second meaning: the opposite of 27-across, ILL AT EASE, so calm

explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27-across, ILL AT EASE; its opposite is a calm, collected state.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of writing music and also an adjective for calm and self-possessed.

clue.text: Old composer left on island in kind way, with excessive care

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer
gently means in a kind, soft manner

explanation.surface: An elderly composer stranded on an island is treated tenderly and very carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Working too hard or too conscientiously, beyond what is needed, is to be overdiligent.

clue.text: Father's expressed appreciation for food

parts.note: pa's, father's in the possessive
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Dad says thanks for his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian dough products such as spaghetti and penne are a staple food.

clue.text: Precipitously reduced energy that marked end of cross-country race?

definitions.text: that marked end of cross-country race?

indicators.note: the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: steeply means precipitously

explanation.surface: A runner's energy drops sharply at the finish of a cross-country race.
explanation.walkthrough: Early steeplechases were horse races across country towards a distant church spire as the finishing point.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire used to be the visible goal of a steeplechase, a race across open country.

clue.text: Man in game that's almost certainly spotted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a piece in the game of ..., called a man
second meaning: one of these tiles nearly always carries spots, unless it is the double blank

explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' allows for the double-blank tile, the one with no spots at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The rectangular tile used in a game of that name is marked with pips, so it is spotted.

clue.text: Changed into a president — inevitable fate?

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into another order

parts.note: these fourteen letters are the fodder that gets rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether becoming head of state was written in the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine that all events are decided in advance, especially by God, is a destiny that cannot be escaped.

clue.text: Group given mission some in government ask for? Certainly

indicators.note: only a portion of the letters within these words is taken, running across them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of government, through ask for, into the start of Certainly

explanation.surface: Asking whether a team with a job is what the government wants, and answering yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A special unit assembled for a particular operation or objective is given this name.

clue.text: Momentum in second eleven

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players

explanation.surface: A reserve football side is building up a head of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up or run out of this is to gain or lose impetus, as with a locomotive's power.

clue.text: Mistakenly declare acquitted

indicators.note: the letters of declare are arranged wrongly, giving a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of this word are the fodder that gets rearranged

explanation.surface: A court wrongly pronounces a defendant not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant found not guilty has had their name exonerated by the verdict.

clue.text: Emotionless university official admitting 500 every year

indicators.note: the university official lets the other pieces in, holding them inside

parts.note: a dean heads a college faculty
D is the Roman numeral for 500
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A cold college administrator lets in five hundred students annually.
explanation.definitionFit: A face or delivery showing no feeling, as in dry comic timing, is described with this word.

clue.text: Form of transport, note, linked with city of Paris mainly

parts.note: me (mi) is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Paris, prince of Troy in Greek legend, belonged to that city

explanation.surface: Describing the Paris underground as a mode of transport tied to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is the Trojan prince, not the French capital, so his city is Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground railway in a city, notably the one in Paris, is called by this name.

clue.text: Girl with sign showing what some people make

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A girl holds up a placard announcing what certain workers earn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed annual pay earned by employees is what people are said to make or draw.

clue.text: Checked, for example, how many votes told

definitions.text: Checked, for example, how many votes
definitions.meaning: first meaning: counted the ballots again
second meaning: narrated, related a story

explanation.walkthrough: The word splits differently for each sense: count again for votes, and recount meaning narrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both counted ballots once more and related or narrated an account.

clue.text: Determinedly set, that guy is going to be not disheartened

parts.note: he'll, the contraction of he will
taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of the word is taken out, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the word's first and last letters remain once its centre is gone

explanation.surface: A fellow resolved to stay cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly resolved to do something, whatever the cost, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Attempt smart merger, meeting as partners

indicators.note: the two words are joined together end to end into one

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Reads like corporate jargon about trying a clever company merger.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting of lovers, so this describes lovers getting together.

clue.text: Person who's stopped working on Scottish island

parts.note: re means on or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone who has given up their job to live on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has left employment for good is called by this word.

clue.text: Form of communication Conservative accomplished

parts.note: an accomplished person is able or skilled

explanation.surface: A skilled Tory politician has mastered a way of communicating.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by undersea wire was a standard method of sending messages abroad.

clue.text: Possible cause of drunken brawl and a lot of gunfire

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a heavy artillery bombardment

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word in two, by analogy with road rage, as fury in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated bombardment of artillery fire is a barrage; read as two words it is pub fury.

clue.text: Periods of good fortune — excited, as a result

parts.note: ups as in ups and downs
hot means aroused or excited

explanation.surface: Lucky spells leave someone thrilled as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or conclusion of events is the upshot.

clue.text: Bone from joint gourmet ultimately put in Spanish dish

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the Spanish dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: the final letter of gourmet, its last one

parts.note: the last letter of this word is the one taken

explanation.surface: A gourmet finds a bit of bone from a joint of meat in his paella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a cut of meat in the cooking scene, but it is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the small bone at the front of the knee joint, and this is its anatomical name.

clue.text: In jail, unchained? One will never be free, they say

definitions.text: One will never be free, they say

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of jail into the start of unchained

explanation.surface: A prisoner wonders about being without chains, though never freed.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'there is no such thing as a free lunch' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a midday meal never comes without some hidden cost to the eater.

clue.text: You can't drive anywhere in this dilapidated Renault

definitions.text: You can't drive anywhere in this

indicators.note: a broken-down car suggests its name's letters falling into a new order

parts.note: the car maker's name supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A clapped-out French car that will not take you anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description of the wrecked car, but it means a gear.
explanation.definitionFit: With the gearbox out of gear the engine runs but the car does not move, so no driving is possible.

clue.text: Rook and duck protected by another bird — or another

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the other bird, sheltered by it

parts.note: a hen is a bird
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A rook and a duck are guarded by a third bird, and maybe a fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or another' means yet another bird: the answer is a fourth bird beyond rook, duck and hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The wading bird with long legs and a long neck is one more bird after the others named.

clue.text: I will josh about area that's not comfortable

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to josh about is to tease, to rib playfully

explanation.surface: Someone vows to rib others about a region that's awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease is an idiom for feeling uncomfortable or uneasy.

clue.text: Like initial problems produced by article on part of course

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: the tee is part of a golf course
a thing is an article or object

explanation.surface: Golf-course snags caused by some item at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Early difficulties in a new venture are called teething troubles, after an infant's first teeth.

clue.text: Most rum toddies must be drunk without one

indicators.note: the letters, like drinkers, are tipsy and so jumbled
the letter for one is taken out of the word

parts.note: the drinks' name supplies the letters, less the one

explanation.surface: Strange hot drinks must be drunk minus one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit in a toddy, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British slang for strange or peculiar, so the superlative is the strangest.
